title: generation of a distinct stored information copy
definition: An actor completes an operation that generates a distinct retained information object reproducing the relevant content of one source information object under a fixed contextual content-equivalence criterion. DAT:000 describes the generated information object; CRE:110 describes that same object's generation by the actor. The source object is the outer target, not the newly generated result. The source and result are distinct tokens even when their relevant content is equal. This operation does not itself remove or modify the source's relevant content. The result is maintained in a contextual store; its location, name, ownership, encoding and physical medium are unspecified. This meaning does not guarantee every bit, file attribute or metadata field is identical unless the contextual criterion includes them. Ongoing aspect views the copying internally without asserting a completed result.
constraints: DAT:000's maintained information object is exactly the artifact generated by CRE:110; the actor is that generation's source.
The outer target is the source information item. The generated result is a distinct existential item, not an alternative name for that source.
One content-equivalence criterion applies to the source and result in the same operation. It is a fixed contextual parameter, not inferred as a numerical or cryptographic guarantee.
Preservation of the source concerns this copying operation; unrelated concurrent changes and future deletion are not ruled out.
excludes: Moving or deleting the source instead of retaining it through the copying operation
A new empty object or an unrelated artifact
Transferring information without a distinct retained copy result
Imitating behavior, making a physical replica, or asserting bitwise and metadata identity without a criterion
near: Nora moved the file and the source entry ceased to exist.
reuse: Reuse this exact copying event before specifying a destination, a named result or a stronger fidelity criterion.
everyday: Creates a distinct stored copy without removing the source

title: retrieval of a latent target representation
definition: A cognizer completes a retrieval transition in which a previously latent mental representation of one distinct target becomes manifest in that cognizer's cognition. MIN:012 describes the retained but nonmanifest representation in the pre-phase; MIN:011 describes that same representation of the same target in the result phase. ORI:110 marks the completed actualization of that manifest condition, not creation of a new target or a new cognizer. This specializes the existing reviewed remember meaning, bringing a previously latent representation into manifest cognition. It does not assert new learning, truth or accuracy of the representation, deliberate effort, spoken expression, emotional familiarity, or continuous awareness. Ongoing aspect views the retrieval internally without asserting its completed result.
constraints: The outer experiencer is the cognizer of both MIN phases; the outer target is the same distinct referent represented in both.
The latent and manifest descriptions are ordered phases of one retrieval, not simultaneous assertions.
The representation is already maintained before retrieval. Actualization concerns its manifest condition, not acquisition of previously absent information.
All phases remain inside the event's tense, negation, modality, aspect and runtime interpretation.
excludes: A representation that merely persists without becoming manifest
Learning or discovering the target for the first time
Truth, accuracy or conscious emotional familiarity inferred from retrieval
Retrieving bytes from storage without cognition, recalling a product, or recalling a sent message
near: Nora retained a representation of Mira but it never came to mind.
reuse: Reuse this retrieval before adding accuracy, a cause, an expressed message or a proposition about the target.
everyday: Brings a previously latent representation back to mind
